posts.hook: The Black Parade, Ranked by You
posts.caption:
not my rankings!! you did this. do you agree?
.

The Black Parade is the most-ranked album on VinylDuel. You sat through it two songs at a time, and Famous Last Words came out on top, with the most first-place votes. Mama is a close second and the most divisive song on the record: a #1 for plenty of people, much lower for others. Welcome to the Black Parade, the song everyone knows, lands third.

The surprise is at the other end. Teenagers, one of the band's biggest hits, is 13th of 14. Nobody put it first.

Stronger misses the top 3 on Graduation, and I Wanna Be Yours is only 5th on AM.

Fall Out Boy fans put Sugar, We're Goin Down 8th, and Crawling sits 11th of 14 on Hybrid Theory.

The community can barely separate Money and Time on The Dark Side of the Moon. Runaway and Power are exactly tied on My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy, and so are R U Mine? and Why'd You Only Call Me When You're High? on AM. Let It Happen just beats New Person, Same Old Mistakes, and Just just beats Fake Plastic Trees.

VinylDuel ranks albums the way you'd argue about them with a friend: two songs at a time. Pick the one you like more, and a sorting algorithm works out your full order in close to the fewest questions possible. A 12-song album takes at most 30 picks, and you can tie, undo, or drag the rest into place yourself.

At the end you get your ranking as a share card, the community's order to compare against, and a link to send a friend so you can see exactly where you disagree.

posts.hook: Three Cheers for Sweet Revenge: The Songs
posts.caption:
the stories behind three cheers 🖤
.
.
.
Three Cheers for Sweet Revenge (2004) is the album that made My Chemical Romance. Three of its biggest songs came with videos by Marc Webb, years before he directed The Amazing Spider-Man.

Helena: Written about Gerard and Mikey Way's grandmother, Elena. The video plays out at her funeral.
You Know What They Do to Guys Like Us in Prison: The longest title on the record, with guest vocals from Bert McCracken of The Used.
I'm Not Okay (I Promise): The breakout single. The video is shot like a high-school movie, with the band as the outcasts.
The Ghost of You: Its video, directed by Marc Webb, recreates a World War II beach landing.
Thank You for the Venom: Not one of the songs from the videos, but the one fans keep coming back to.

posts.hook: Ten: The Songs
posts.caption:
the stories behind ten
.
.
.
Ten (1991) is Pearl Jam's debut, released a month before Nevermind.

Once: The opener. It began as one of Stone Gossard's instrumental demos, on the same tape that became Alive.
Even Flow: Notoriously hard to get right in the studio. The band recorded it again and again.
Alive: Eddie Vedder wrote the words to a demo tape he'd been sent, before he had even met the band.
Black: Never released as a single. The band said no, because it was too personal.
Jeremy: Based on a real 1991 news story about a Texas teenager. The video won four MTV awards, including Video of the Year.

Thriller (1982) is still the best-selling album of all time. Five of its songs, and where they came from.

Wanna Be Startin' Somethin': The opener. Its closing chant is borrowed from Manu Dibango's 1972 song Soul Makossa.
Thriller: Ends with a spoken-word section by horror actor Vincent Price.
Beat It: Eddie Van Halen played the guitar solo, and did it for free.
Billie Jean: Michael first did the moonwalk performing it on Motown 25 in 1983.
Human Nature: Written by Toto's Steve Porcaro, with lyrics by John Bettis.
